passage:
"Someone must have called already," Pankaj said, looking at the scooter lying on its side near the crossing and the rider on the road. About thirty people stood in a ring. Some held up phones.
"Did you call?" asked Sarika.
"No. I thought..."
"Everyone thinks that." She pointed. "You, in the blue shirt, call 112 and tell them the crossing near the bakery. You, with the cap, stop the cars. Pankaj, stay by him and talk. Nobody move him."
Pankaj crouched. "Can you hear me? Help is coming." The man in the blue shirt was already speaking to the operator.

qa.a: The scooter was lying on its side near the crossing.

qa.q: What is Pankaj feeling when saying that someone must have called already?
qa.a: Pankaj is probably shocked and unsure, and hopes that someone else has taken charge, which lets Pankaj avoid acting.

qa.q: What broke the crowd's waiting, and why did it work?
qa.a: Sarika pointed at specific people and gave each a task, such as calling 112 and stopping cars, so nobody could assume someone else would.

qa.q: How might the rider feel hearing Pankaj say "Help is coming"?
qa.a: The rider might feel frightened but comforted that a person is nearby speaking calmly, instead of a ring of people only watching.

grounding: Shows a teenager in a crowd assuming someone else has called for help until one person names who should call.

passage: I was at the bus stop by the flyover when a man near the shelter dropped to the ground. A crowd formed. I stood at the back, holding my school bag, thinking someone had surely phoned. Phones were up, but I could not see anyone speaking into one. Then Minakshi, who sells tea at the stall, called across, "You with the bag. Call 112. Say the bus stop by the flyover." My hands shook, but I dialled. The operator asked simple questions and told me to stay on the line. Minakshi sat beside the man and kept talking to him. I kept thinking how long I would have stood there. Jagdish

qa.q: Who told the narrator to call 112?
qa.a: Minakshi, who sells tea at the stall, told Jagdish to call 112.

qa.q: What was Jagdish feeling while standing at the back holding the school bag?
qa.a: Jagdish was probably unsure and frozen, assuming that someone else had surely phoned.
Minakshi picked Jagdish out of the crowd and gave a clear instruction to call 112 and say the bus stop by the flyover.

qa.q: How might Minakshi have seen the crowd standing around?
qa.a: Minakshi could see that people had phones up but nobody speaking to an operator, so gave a direct order to one person.

grounding: Shows a teenager in a crowd assuming someone else has called until a person is named to call.
